verdict_reason: Engine 0.1.0.dev13 (2026-11-08) adds the audit's Phase 2 fixes (retrieval at corpus scale: applicability before the candidate caps, the current action's caution among many lessons, the query time at 10,000 heads, a store that loses FTS5; decision 0045) to 0.1.0.dev12's Phase 1 fixes (the worker's scheduling, crash visibility, review retries, retention and forgetting; decision 0044) and 0.1.0.dev11's Phase 0 fixes (docs/audits/2026-11-06-memory-system-audit.md): secrets in split command arguments, text-redaction gaps, a loopback request routed through a named proxy, and lost partitioned messages. Those change capture, message partitioning, the API transport and what context is delivered, so the smoke gate that passed on 0.1.0.dev10 is re-run on the fixed engine before release. Nine live gates failed and the tenth passed the smoke quality gate with the owner's recorded labels; the release stays blocked on a Linux live run (macOS is not certified for the preview, decision 0041), release signing and the owner's go-ahead to publish (the license is GPL-3.0-only, decision 0042). The first (2026-10-26): the installed host updated itself mid-run, the machine slept, and update_task replies hit their output allowance under a reasoning curator. The second (2026-10-29, engine 0.1.0.dev1, Claude Code 2.1.310 live-certified): no curator call hit the output cap, but the lid was closed overnight and Wi-Fi dropped on waking, R4's working agents wrote CLAUDE.md in both arms, R4's stale fact was delivered without a freshness label, and fresh-session reuse and the changed-condition revision were not shown; live §5.1 support and recall await reviewer labels. The third (2026-10-31, engine 0.1.0.dev4): complete and clean, with every wait quiet, no suspension and all five demonstrations; it failed on unlabeled claims, and the model-drafted labels put useful recall at 5/8 and failed-approach recall at 1/3, under target whatever the judgment calls (decision 0035). The fourth (2026-11-01, engine 0.1.0.dev5, 6 slots, 45 min): complete and clean again; it failed on R4's conflict label (0/1: a user's statement about storage was kept as a decision without its file, decision 0036) and 31 unlabeled items, whose drafted labels give support 22/23, useful recall 7/7 and failed-approach recall 2/2. The fifth (2026-11-01, engine 0.1.0.dev6, 6 slots, 48 min): complete and clean, with every measure that needs no labels met, conflict/uncertainty preservation included (1/1); drafted labels give support 18/18, useful recall 6/7 and failed-approach recall 1/2, and the owner accepted the recommendation that L1's pipe-hidden failure, which stayed a candidate after review, was missed, so it failed on failed-approach recall (decision 0037). The sixth (2026-11-02, engine 0.1.0.dev7, 6 slots, 43 min): all 24 trials ran without error or contamination and the three workload days within budget; decision 0037 worked (L1's pipe-hidden failure was admitted as a condition), but two user declarations were lost to code's strict checks (L3's refused for its citation, L2's most likely malformed), so drafted labels give useful recall 5/7 whatever the judgment calls and the forgetting demonstration had no claim to forget; most update_task replies also fail validation (decision 0038). The seventh (2026-11-03, engine 0.1.0.dev8, 6 slots, 48 min): all 24 trials ran without error or contamination and the three workload days within budget; L3's declaration was admitted and forgotten, but the fresh session after the forget was delivered text holding the limit, from a source the record did not keep (decision 0028 item 29), so the forgetting demonstration failed; as drafted, the labels meet every labeled measure (support 14/14, useful recall 6/7, failed-approach recall 2/2) by two judgment calls; most update_task replies appended bare strings where a field takes a supported text (decision 0039). The eighth (2026-11-03, engine 0.1.0.dev9, 6 slots, 47 min): all 24 trials ran without error or contamination and the three workload days within budget; all five demonstrations were shown; decision 0039 cured the refused replies (one malformed operation in 45 update_task calls); as drafted, the labels meet every labeled measure (support 14/14, useful recall 7/7, failed-approach recall 2/2); it failed only on incorrect confident guidance, because R3's oracle read the candidate's "$700 per month (updated from $600)" as the stale limit (fixed for the next run, decision 0028 item 30). The ninth (2026-11-04, engine 0.1.0.dev9, 6 slots, 43 min): all 24 trials ran without error or contamination and the three workload days within budget; all five demonstrations were shown and every measure that needs no labels is met; with the owner's recorded labels (two model reviews, adopted where they agreed, and the owner's rule that support is judged at admission, decision 0028 item 31) it failed on supported precision, 22/24, because two claims overstated a detail; useful recall 6/7 and failed-approach recall 2/2 were met. The tenth (2026-11-04, engine 0.1.0.dev10, 6 slots, 48 min): all 24 trials ran without error or contamination and the three workload days within budget; all five demonstrations were shown and every measure that needs no labels is met; with the owner's recorded labels (two model reviews, adopted where they agreed; the owner decided the two differences, R2's import lesson evidence_absent as for the ninth gate's L1 #1, and L4's interpreter-path claim unsupported) it passed: support 21/22, useful recall 7/7, failed-approach recall 2/2. It is the first live pass, with one trial per arm, gold written by the coding agent (not held out), labels not independent of SYSTEM_SPEC §7, support one claim above its target and R2's failure lesson untested. A scripted/recorded run is never a pass

tools/build_release.py checks the runtime closure of requirements.lock with each package's declared license against docs/release/DEPENDENCIES.json, the wheel's contents against src/recalith, and the absence of foreign copyright headers (no upstream source is adapted, so no THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md ships). The project's own license is GPL-3.0-only (decision 0042): pyproject.toml declares it, docs/release/DEPENDENCIES.json records it, and the wheel and sdist carry LICENSE.

tools/measure_release_latency.py and tools/measure_worker_latency.py run the §7 populations per native platform: this container and .github/workflows/measure.yml on Linux, macOS and Windows runners. Every healthy target is met on every platform on the final code (b3f1f1f) in two full measure runs (21 and 24). Hook spawn-to-exit p95: Linux 53.0/59.3 ms warm and 46.6/59.8 ms cold; macOS 92.0/126.1 warm and 62.9/81.7 cold; Windows 138.7/135.0 warm and 137.8/148.1 cold. Warm delivered ≥ 0.998 and cold 1.0 everywhere. This container: 108.5 ms warm and 105.9 ms cold, 500/500 delivered. Typed event to working state, p95 with 5 s idle polling: Linux 4.48/4.47 s; macOS 4.55/4.39 s; Windows 4.82/4.92 s (n=20 each); Windows 4.75 and 4.62 s in two 60-trial runs (22 and 23); this container 4.74 s (n=100). Idle worker over 600 s: under 0.24 % of one core and ≤ 47 MiB everywhere. Decision 0022 attributed the earlier Windows typed-state misses. The measurement planned arrivals from a stale idle status and read poll durations one poll late, which made a cadence drift appear that the worker does not have. The remaining Windows outliers are single ingesting polls stalled by the runner's storage (1–5 s), and the WAL checkpoint was moved off the typed-state path. Targets, n, denominators and the arrival model are unchanged (the arrival planning is now stricter). Live trials stay with B1.

Every kill/restart family at RECALITH_CRASH_REPS=20 (100 is for a release candidate, which this is not): 13 families, 128 failpoint cases × 20 reps, 128 passed in 6343.01 s on Linux (Task 18 checkpoint). The retention family gained retention.after_record_aging, and a deliberate mutation there was caught only by this matrix. macOS and Windows run the same families at the default 3 repetitions in CI; the 20-repetition run is Linux only. Decision 0022 added worker.before_checkpoint and worker.after_checkpoint. Every worker family plus capture (125 cases) passed again at 20 repetitions on the final tree (71 passed in 3044.07 s and 54 passed in 2886.46 s).
tools/build_release.py and .github/workflows/release.yml build the wheel and sdist with SHA-256 digests and a release manifest. They are unsigned, and nothing is tagged or published.
